claim: Simultaneous patch-clamp recordings from multiple neurons offer the highest temporal and subthreshold resolution to analyse local synaptic connectivity.
source: Simultaneous patch-clamp recordings from multiple neurons offer the highest temporal and subthreshold resolution to analyse local synaptic connectivity.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the abstract about the capabilities of multipatch recordings.

claim: The multipatch setup can record up to 10 neurons simultaneously.
source: We introduce an in vitro multipatch setup with an automated pipette pressure and cleaning system facilitating recordings of up to 10 neurons simultaneously and sequential patching of additional neurons.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract as a capability of the introduced system.

claim: The method allowed probing of 150 synaptic connections between 17 neurons in one human cortical slice.
source: This method will facilitate the systematic analysis of microcircuits and allow unprecedented assessment of inter-individual variability.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 6A showing recordings from 17 neurons.

claim: The method enabled screening of over 600 connections in tissue from a single patient.
source: We present hardware and software solutions that increase the usability, speed and data throughput of multipatch experiments which allowed probing of 150 synaptic connections between 17 neurons in one human cortical slice and screening of over 600 connections in tissue from a single patient.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6F showing 336-694 tested connections per patient.

claim: Feedforward information flow between cortical layers is stereotypical.
source: While it is well established that feedforward information flow between the cortical layers is rather stereotypical (Douglas and Martin, 2004), intralaminar connectivity between different classes of neurons is more complicated and heterogeneous across brain regions (Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Steiner et al., 2019; Song et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Douglas and Martin, 2004.

claim: Intralaminar connectivity between different classes of neurons is more complicated and heterogeneous across brain regions.
source: While it is well established that feedforward information flow between the cortical layers is rather stereotypical (Douglas and Martin, 2004), intralaminar connectivity between different classes of neurons is more complicated and heterogeneous across brain regions (Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Steiner et al., 2019; Song et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations (Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Steiner et al., 2019; Song et al., 2005).

claim: It remains unclear how observed microcircuit topologies generalize across species.
source: Furthermore, it remains as yet unclear how observed microcircuit topologies generalize across species, or whether inter-individual variability can be observed at the level of neuronal microcircuits.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: Specific cellular and synaptic properties in the human central nervous system have been described.
source: While specific cellular and synaptic properties in the human central nervous system have been described (Kalmbach et al., 2018; Molnár et al., 2016; Szegedi et al., 2016), distinctive features at the microcircuit level have yet to be resolved (Seeman et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kalmbach et al., 2018; Molnár et al., 2016; Szegedi et al., 2016.

claim: Distinctive features at the microcircuit level in humans have yet to be resolved.
source: While specific cellular and synaptic properties in the human central nervous system have been described (Kalmbach et al., 2018; Molnár et al., 2016; Szegedi et al., 2016), distinctive features at the microcircuit level have yet to be resolved (Seeman et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap with citation to Seeman et al., 2018.

claim: Availability of human brain tissue is scarce.
source: Availability of human brain tissue is scarce, making it, at present, necessary to pool data across patients.
evidence: Stated as a practical constraint in the introduction.

claim: Pooling data across patients is problematic considering the high diversity between patients with respect to different environmental and genetic background, medical history and medication.
source: This is problematic considering the high diversity between patients with respect to different environmental and genetic background, medical history and medication.
evidence: Stated as a logical concern based on known patient variability.

claim: Multiple whole-cell patch-clamp recordings represent the gold standard method to dissect microcircuits compared to various other approaches.
source: To dissect microcircuits, multiple whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (multipatch) still represent the gold standard method compared to various other approaches (Hochbaum et al., 2014; Packer et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as an established fact with citations to Hochbaum et al., 2014; Packer et al., 2015.

claim: Multipatch can reliably detect unitary excitatory and inhibitory synaptic connections due to its sub-millisecond and subthreshold resolution.
source: This method can reliably detect unitary excitatory and inhibitory synaptic connections due to its sub-millisecond and subthreshold resolution (Geiger et al., 1997).
evidence: Stated as a capability with citation to Geiger et al., 1997.

claim: Multipatch allows for detailed electrophysiological and morphological characterization of recorded neurons.
source: In addition, it allows for detailed electrophysiological and morphological characterization of recorded neurons and can be used across species without the need for genetic modifications in contrast to optogenetics or calcium imaging (Markram et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated as a capability with citation to Markram et al., 2004.

claim: Multipatch can be used across species without the need for genetic modifications in contrast to optogenetics or calcium imaging.
source: In addition, it allows for detailed electrophysiological and morphological characterization of recorded neurons and can be used across species without the need for genetic modifications in contrast to optogenetics or calcium imaging (Markram et al., 2004).
evidence: Stated as an advantage with citation to Markram et al., 2004.

claim: Increasing the number of simultaneously recorded neurons can increase the number of probed synaptic connections considerably.
source: Increasing the number of simultaneously recorded neurons can increase the number of probed synaptic connections considerably and generate larger sample sizes from fewer experiments.
evidence: Stated as a logical consequence and demonstrated in Figure 4A.

claim: Various groups were able to increase the number of simultaneous recordings.
source: Various groups were able to increase the number of simultaneous recordings (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Perin et al., 2011; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wang et al., 2015), but the operation of multiple manipulators is challenging.
evidence: Supported by multiple citations (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Perin et al., 2011; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wang et al., 2015).

claim: The operation of multiple manipulators is challenging.
source: Various groups were able to increase the number of simultaneous recordings (Guzman et al., 2016; Jiang et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2017; Perin et al., 2011; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wang et al., 2015), but the operation of multiple manipulators is challenging.
evidence: Stated as a practical challenge in the introduction.

claim: Several approaches have been reported that automate the patch-clamp process, utilizing automated pressure control systems and algorithms for manipulator movements.
source: To address this, several approaches have been reported that automate the patch-clamp process, utilizing automated pressure control systems and algorithms for manipulator movements guided by visual or electrical signals (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wu et al., 2016; Kolb et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012; Perin and Markram, 2013; Wu et al., 2016; Kolb et al., 2019).

claim: Eight or more manipulators on one setup are currently used by only a few labs.
source: However, while simultaneous recordings of up to four neurons are becoming increasingly popular, eight or more manipulators on one setup are currently used by only a few labs, missing out on the opportunity to maximize the potential of this method.
evidence: Stated as an observation about current practice in the field.

claim: Cleaning pipettes for immediate reuse increases the size of recorded neuron clusters.
source: Cleaning pipettes for immediate reuse increases the size of recorded neuron clusters and enables a more complete view of the microcircuit.
evidence: Stated as a benefit and demonstrated in Figure 5B-C showing increased cluster sizes.

claim: The maximum number of simultaneously recorded neurons is highly limited by the spatial constraints imposed by the manipulators.
source: The maximum number of simultaneously recorded neurons is highly limited by the spatial constraints imposed by the manipulators.
evidence: Stated as a practical limitation in the introduction.

claim: Pipette cleaning has been implemented for automated patch-clamp of single neurons in vivo and in vitro.
source: This technique has already been implemented for automated patch-clamp of single neurons in vivo (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018) and in vitro (Kolb et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018 and Kolb et al., 2019.

claim: Sequential recordings from multiple cells using the same pipette would overcome the limitation on maximum cluster size given by the number of manipulators in use.
source: Sequential recordings from multiple cells using the same pipette would also overcome the limitation on maximum cluster size given by the number of manipulators in use.
evidence: Stated as a logical benefit of the pipette cleaning approach.

claim: The approach increases the rate of complete clusters and decreases experimental time.
source: Here, we show that this approach and further optimizations increase the rate of complete clusters, decrease experimental time and enable sequential patching of additional neurons.
evidence: Stated as a finding and supported by data in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Probing of up to 600 synaptic connections in human brain slices in one day is possible with two setups.
source: We demonstrate that probing of up to 600 synaptic connections in human brain slices in one day is possible with two setups, allowing analysis of microcircuits at the level of individual patients.
evidence: Stated as a demonstration and supported by data in Figure 6F showing 336-694 tested connections per patient.

claim: Ten Sensapex uMp-Micromanipulators were arranged on a setup with a Nikon Eclipse FN1 microscope using a custom-made stage.
source: We arranged 10 Sensapex uMp-Micromanipulators on a setup with a Nikon Eclipse FN1 microscope using a custom-made stage which was fabricated by a commercial metal workshop (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods and shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: A setup with 8 Scientifica PatchStar manipulators was successfully established on a custom-made stage with a Scientifica SliceScope microscope.
source: We also successfully established a setup with 8 Scientifica PatchStar manipulators on a custom-made stage with a Scientifica SliceScope microscope (Figure 1D; Peng et al., 2017).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods with citation to Peng et al., 2017 and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The custom stages consist of a 10 mm aluminium sheet for stability glued to a 1 mm stainless steel sheet to create a ferromagnetic surface for cable routing using magnets.
source: Our custom stages consist of a 10 mm aluminium sheet for stability glued to a 1 mm stainless steel sheet to create a ferromagnetic surface for cable routing using magnets.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing the custom stage construction.

claim: A 27° approach angle was found to be optimal for the custom-made recording chamber.
source: We found 27° to be optimal for our custom-made recording chamber, which is positioned on an elevated platform.
evidence: Stated as an empirical finding in the methods section.

claim: Five MultiClamp 700B amplifiers were connected to one digitizer enabling simultaneous recording of 10 channels.
source: On the 10-manipulator setup, five MultiClamp 700B amplifiers (Molecular Devices) were connected to one digitizer (Power1401-3A with Signal extension from Cambridge Electronic Design) enabling simultaneous recording of 10 channels within the corresponding commercial software Signal (Table 1).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing the hardware configuration.

claim: A routing device was developed to increase the number of DAC output channels from 8 to 10 on the 10-manipulator setup.
source: We achieved this by a simple routing device that can switch between channels enabling four headstages to receive stimulation from only two DAC outputs (for details and limitations of the routing device see Appendix 3—figure 11).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing the solution to hardware limitations.

claim: The automated pressure system can be built within a week with basic electrical equipment and does not require extensive technical skills.
source: It can be built within a week with basic electrical equipment and does not require extensive technical skills.
evidence: Stated as a practical assessment of the construction requirements.

claim: LOW pressure is set at 20 mbar for continuous outflow of pipette solution during the idle state in the bath to prevent clogging of the tip.
source: We set one pressure regulator at 20 mbar (LOW) for continuous outflow of pipette solution during the idle state in the bath to prevent clogging of the tip.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing the pressure system settings.

claim: HIGH pressure of 70 mbar is applied for moving through the slice to approach the cell.
source: We apply 70 mbar (HIGH) for moving through the slice to approach the cell.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing the pressure system settings.

claim: Fine adjustment of suction duration and strength is crucial to achieve maximum success rate.
source: We believe that this is a crucial part of the patching process which needs fine adjustment regarding the duration and strength of suction to achieve maximum success rate (up to 88% on six-manipulator setup, see results on performance below).
evidence: Stated as an assessment based on experience and supported by success rate data.

claim: Fully automated in-vitro patch-clamp algorithms have reported a relatively low success rate of 43% using a single pipette.
source: Compared to this, reports on fully automated in-vitro patch-clamp algorithms have reported a relatively low success rate of 43% using a single pipette (Wu and Chubykin, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wu and Chubykin, 2017.

claim: The entire cleaning process takes approximately 1 minute and can be executed for multiple pipettes at the same time.
source: The entire cleaning process takes approximately 1 minute and can be executed for multiple pipettes at the same time.
evidence: Stated as a practical characteristic of the cleaning procedure.

claim: Alconox contains 10–20% sodium linear alkylbenzene sulfonate (LAS), which affects Glycin-, GABAA- and GluR6-mediated currents at concentrations around 0.001%.
source: Alconox contains 10–20% sodium linear alkylbenzene sulfonate (LAS), which affects Glycin-, GABAA- and GluR6-mediated currents at concentrations around 0.001% (Machu et al., 1998).
evidence: Supported by citation to Machu et al., 1998.

claim: No significant amount of LAS could be detected in the pipette solution after the cleaning cycles.
source: Since it has already been shown that no significant amount of LAS could be detected in the pipette solution after the cleaning cycles (Kolb et al., 2016), the remaining potential source of contamination is residual detergent adhering to the outside surface of the pipette tip.
evidence: Supported by citation to Kolb et al., 2016.

claim: At least 25 µl Alconox would be needed to reach the critical LAS concentration of 0.001% in the extracellular solution, assuming a recording bath volume of 1 ml and a LAS concentration of 20% in the 2% Alconox solution.
source: A volume of at least 25 µl Alconox would be needed to reach the critical LAS concentration of 0.001% in the extracellular solution, assuming a recording bath volume of 1 ml and a LAS concentration of 20% in the 2% Alconox solution.
evidence: Stated as a calculation based on known concentrations and volumes.

claim: The adherent Alconox solution on a pipette tip is estimated to be less than 0.2 µl.
source: We estimate the adherent Alconox solution on a pipette tip to be less than 0.2 µl, considering that the total volume of intracellular solution inside a pipette is usually less than 15 µl.
evidence: Stated as an estimate based on pipette volume considerations.

claim: No evidence was found for a systematic change in cellular or synaptic physiology after pipette cleaning in rat neurons.
source: While we observed some variability between different recordings, we found no evidence for a systematic change in cellular or synaptic physiology (p>0.05 in all comparisons using repeated measures ANOVA, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: Stated as a finding from control experiments with statistical support (p>0.05).

claim: The mean relative difference for all parameters were between 0% and 10% after pipette cleaning in rat neurons.
source: The mean relative difference for all parameters were between 0% and 10%.
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding from the control experiments.

claim: More than 10 successful 'repatches' using the same patch pipette were possible while no change in the electrophysiological properties of the cells was observed.
source: In this study, more than 10 successful 'repatches' using the same patch pipette were possible while no change in the electrophysiological properties of the cells was observed.
evidence: Stated as a finding from a previous study (Kolb et al., 2016) that was implemented in this work.

claim: The success rate of patch attempts after cleaning in rat experiments was 98%.
source: Thus, the success rate of patch attempts after cleaning in these experiments was 98% (53 successful whole-cell recordings out of 54 patch attempts).
evidence: Stated as a calculated result from the control experiments.

claim: On a setup with six manipulators, an average of 5.3 ± 0.7 successful recordings per cluster were obtained with an average of 23 ± 7 tested connections.
source: On a setup with six manipulators, we obtained on average 5.3 ± 0.7 successful recordings per cluster with an average of 23 ± 7 tested connections (mean ± standard deviation, n = 30).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding from performance analysis.

claim: The six-manipulator setup achieved an average success rate of 88 ± 12%.
source: This corresponds to an average success rate of 88 ± 12% which is calculated as the ratio of successfully recorded cells to the maximum number of pipettes available per cluster (Figure 4B).
evidence: Stated as a calculated result and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: After scaling up to eight pipettes, an average of 6.8 ± 1 cells were recorded (success rate 85 ± 13%) which increased the mean number of tested connections to 41 ± 13.
source: After scaling up to eight pipettes, we could record from 6.8 ± 1 cells on average (success rate 85 ± 13%) which increased the mean number of tested connections to 41 ± 13 (n = 33).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding from performance analysis.

claim: On the setup with 10 pipettes, an average of 7.9 ± 1.1 neurons were recorded with 56 ± 17 tested connections, representing a success rate of 79 ± 11%.
source: On our setup with 10 pipettes, we recorded on average from 7.9 ± 1.1 neurons with 56 ± 17 tested connections which represents a further drop of the success rate to 79 ± 11% (n = 10).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding from performance analysis.

claim: The total experimental time needed before the start of recording rose from 36.6 ± 2.3 min (eight pipettes) to 46.1 ± 4.6 min (10 pipettes).
source: Concurrently, the total experimental time needed before the start of recording the electrophysiological properties of the neurons rose from 36.6 ± 2.3 min (eight pipettes) to 46.1 ± 4.6 min (10 pipettes), mostly due to increasing time needed to approach and patch the cells (16.8 ± 2.7 min vs 25.8 ± 2.2 min, Figure 4D).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The clean-to-complete strategy increased the average cluster size on setups with 8 and 10 pipettes to 7.8 ± 0.4 (97% ± 5% success rate) and 9.2 ± 0.6 (92% ± 6% success rate), respectively.
source: This clean-to-complete strategy increased the average cluster size on our setups with 8 and 10 pipettes to 7.8 ± 0.4 (97% ± 5% success rate, n = 16) and 9.2 ± 0.6 (92% ± 6% success rate, n = 9), respectively (Figure 5B).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Using both cleaning strategies during rodent experiments on the eight-pipette setup with two recorded slices per animal, the number of tested connections increased from 140 ± 24 to 244 ± 52 on average per animal.
source: Using both strategies during rodent experiments on the eight-pipette setup with two to recorded slices per animal, we could increase the number of tested connections from 140 ± 24 to 244 ± 52 on average per animal (Figure 5D, mean ± standard deviation, n = 6 animals).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The distance distribution in the initial cluster (median 84 µm, IQR 61–110 µm) was similar and not systematically shifted compared to the second (median 85 µm, IQR 62–109 µm) and third round of recording (median 84 µm, IQR 60–107 µm).
source: The distance distribution in the initial cluster (median 84 µm, IQR 61–110 µm, 278 pairs) was similar and not systematically shifted compared to the second (median 85 µm, IQR 62–109 µm, 218 pairs) and third round of recording (median 84 µm, IQR 60–107 µm, 166 pairs).
evidence: Stated as a quantitative finding from distance analysis.

claim: With two rounds of clean-to-extend, up to 17 neighboring neurons were recorded in one human slice.
source: With two rounds of clean-to-extend, we were able to record electrophysiological properties and the synaptic connections of up to 17 neighboring neurons in one human slice (Figure 6A).
evidence: Stated as a finding and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Using two setups simultaneously, up to 99 neurons were recorded and 300 to 700 potential synaptic connections were probed from individual patients within the first 24 hr after slicing.
source: Using two setups simultaneously, we were able to record from up to 99 neurons and thereby probe 300 to 700 potential synaptic connections from individual patients within the first 24 hr after slicing.
evidence: Stated as a finding and supported by data in Figure 6E-F.

claim: Excitatory connectivity between pyramidal cells in human cortical layer 2/3 ranged from 12.9% to 17.7%.
source: We found excitatory connectivity between pyramidal cells in human cortical layer 2/3 ranging from 12.9% to 17.7% which is similar to those reported previously (Boldog et al., 2018; Seeman et al., 2018; Szegedi et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated as a finding with comparison to previous studies (Boldog et al., 2018; Seeman et al., 2018; Szegedi et al., 2016).

claim: The inter-individual differences in connectivity were not statistically different from each other (Pat. 1 vs 2, p=0.08; Pat. 1 vs 3, p=0.26; Pat. 2 vs 3, p=0.41).
source: The inter-individual differences were not statistically different from each other (Pat. 1 vs 2, p=0.08; Pat. 1 vs 3, p=0.26; Pat. 2 vs 3, p=0.41) while they were statistically equivalent within a range of −5 and 9.5% (Pat. 1 vs 2, 4.9% [0.3% 9.5%], Pat. 1 vs 3, 3.1% [-1.5% 7.7%], Pat. 2 vs 3, −1.8% [−5% 1.5%], proportion difference [90% confidence interval of difference]).
evidence: Stated as a statistical finding from the human connectivity data.

claim: Manual adjustments during the visually guided approach of the cell and the fine-tuned application of pressure yielded higher success rates (88%/85%/79% on the 6-/8-/10-manipulator setup) compared to a fully automated system with pipette cleaning and machine vision which reported a success rate of 43% to 51%.
source: We found that manual adjustments during the visually guided approach of the cell and the fine-tuned application of pressure to obtain a whole-cell configuration yielded higher success rates (88%/85 % / 79% on the 6-/8-/10-manipulator setup) compared to a fully automated system with pipette cleaning and machine vision which reported a success rate of 43% to 51% (Wu et al., 2016; Kolb et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with citations to Wu et al., 2016 and Kolb et al., 2019.

claim: The semi-automated pipette positioning approach was faster (53/55 s per pipette on 8-/10-manipulator setup) than the fully automated method described in Wu et al. (2016) (103 s using one pipette).
source: Our semi-automated pipette positioning approach was faster (53/55 s per pipette on 8-/10-manipulator setup) than the fully automated method described in Wu et al. (2016) (103 s using one pipette) while the time needed to manually approach the cell and establish a whole-cell configuration was slightly higher (126/154 s per pipette on 8-/10-manipulator setup vs 120 s).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with citation to Wu et al., 2016.

claim: A previous study has demonstrated an automatic synapse detection algorithm using a support vector machine classifier that achieved an accuracy of 95%.
source: For connectivity studies, a previous study has demonstrated an automatic synapse detection algorithm using a support vector machine classifier that achieved an accuracy of 95% (Seeman et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Seeman et al., 2018.

claim: Underestimation of synaptic connectivity in slice experiments is an important concern and subject to ongoing debate.
source: Underestimation of synaptic connectivity in slice experiments is an important concern and subject to ongoing debate (Jiang et al., 2015; Jiang et al., 2016; Barth et al., 2016).
evidence: Stated as a known issue with citations to Jiang et al., 2015; Jiang et al., 2016; Barth et al., 2016.

claim: Simulations of slicing effects on connection probability have shown a correction factor between 1.3 to 1.7.
source: Anatomical reconstructions can help to assess the extent of axon cutting and refine the optimal slicing angle while simulations of slicing effects on connection probability have shown a correction factor between 1.3 to 1.7 (Levy and Reyes, 2012; Jiang et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Levy and Reyes, 2012 and Jiang et al., 2016.

claim: In vivo recordings with no cutting effects found a connection probability of 6.7% between pyramidal cells in the mouse barrel cortex compared to 9.3% in slice experiments.
source: On the other hand, in vivo recordings with no cutting effects found a connection probability of 6.7% between pyramidal cells in the mouse barrel cortex compared to 9.3% in slice experiments (Jouhanneau et al., 2018; Lefort et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jouhanneau et al., 2018 and Lefort et al., 2009.

claim: A previous study used simulations of background noise to determine the detection limits, reporting a correction factor of 1.1 for connection probability.
source: To address this, a previous study has used simulations of background noise to determine the detection limits, reporting a correction factor of 1.1 for connection probability (Seeman et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Seeman et al., 2018.

claim: All-optical approaches using channelrhodopsins to stimulate individual neurons and fluorescent calcium or voltage indicators to measure their responses can be used to probe connectivity of a higher number of cells than the multipatch approach.
source: All-optical approaches using channelrhodopsins to stimulate individual neurons and fluorescent calcium or voltage indicators to measure their responses can be used to probe connectivity of a higher number of cells than the multipatch approach (Emiliani et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated as a comparison with citation to Emiliani et al., 2015.

claim: Simultaneous optical stimulation and recording using calcium indicators have been performed in up to 20 neurons.
source: Simultaneous optical stimulation and recording using calcium indicators have been performed in up to 20 neurons (Packer et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to Packer et al., 2015.

claim: Calcium transients cannot resolve single action potentials or subthreshold postsynaptic signals, potentially missing monosynaptic connections.
source: However, calcium transients cannot resolve single action potentials or subthreshold postsynaptic signals, potentially missing monosynaptic connections.
evidence: Stated as a limitation of calcium imaging based on known properties.

claim: Voltage indicators can resolve subthreshold signals with higher temporal resolution than calcium imaging and have been shown to detect monosynaptic connections combined with optical stimulation in organotypical slices.
source: Voltage indicators can resolve subthreshold signals with higher temporal resolution than calcium imaging and have been shown to detect monosynaptic connections combined with optical stimulation in organotypical slices (Hochbaum et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hochbaum et al., 2014.

claim: Multipatch in vivo is technically very challenging and thus far limited to a maximum of four pipettes.
source: While calcium imaging can also be applied in vivo, multipatch in this condition is technically very challenging and thus far limited to a maximum of four pipettes (Jouhanneau et al., 2018; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018).
evidence: Stated as a technical limitation with citations to Jouhanneau et al., 2018 and Kodandaramaiah et al., 2018.

claim: Two-photon glutamate uncaging allows mapping of monosynaptic inputs from 10 to 50 presynaptic neurons onto a single patched neuron.
source: Stimulation through a high-density multielectrode array or two-photon glutamate uncaging allows mapping of monosynaptic inputs from 10 to 50 presynaptic neurons onto a single patched neuron (Fino and Yuste, 2011; Jäckel et al., 2017), while two-photon optogenetic stimulation can probe connections from up to 200 presynaptic neurons in a single experiment (Izquierdo-Serra et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Fino and Yuste, 2011 and Jäckel et al., 2017.

claim: Two-photon optogenetic stimulation can probe connections from up to 200 presynaptic neurons in a single experiment.
source: Stimulation through a high-density multielectrode array or two-photon glutamate uncaging allows mapping of monosynaptic inputs from 10 to 50 presynaptic neurons onto a single patched neuron (Fino and Yuste, 2011; Jäckel et al., 2017), while two-photon optogenetic stimulation can probe connections from up to 200 presynaptic neurons in a single experiment (Izquierdo-Serra et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Izquierdo-Serra et al., 2018.

claim: Human tissue was acquired from temporal lobe resections of patients with pharmacoresistant temporal lobe epilepsy.
source: Human tissue was acquired from temporal lobe resections of patients with pharmacoresistant temporal lobe epilepsy.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section.

claim: All patients gave written consent for the scientific use of the resected tissue.
source: All patients gave a written consent for the scientific use of the resected tissue.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section regarding ethical procedures.

claim: All procedures adhered to ethical requirements and were in accordance to the respective ethical approval (EA2/111/14).
source: All procedures adhered to ethical requirements and were in accordance to the respective ethical approval (EA2/111/14).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section regarding ethical procedures.

claim: Acute brain slices were prepared from 19 to 35 days old transgenic Wistar rats expressing Venus-YFP under the VGAT promotor.
source: Acute brain slices were prepared from 19 to 35 days old transgenic Wistar rats expressing Venus-YFP under the VGAT promotor (Peng et al., 2017; Uematsu et al., 2008) or from 21 to 42 days old male C57BL/6N mice (Böhm et al., 2015).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section with citations to Peng et al., 2017 and Uematsu et al., 2008.

claim: Acute brain slices were prepared from 21 to 42 days old male C57BL/6N mice.
source: Acute brain slices were prepared from 19 to 35 days old transgenic Wistar rats expressing Venus-YFP under the VGAT promotor (Peng et al., 2017; Uematsu et al., 2008) or from 21 to 42 days old male C57BL/6N mice (Böhm et al., 2015).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section with citation to Böhm et al., 2015.

claim: Tissue samples were transferred to the laboratory within 30 to 40 min in cooled sucrose based aCSF enriched with carbogen.
source: In brief, tissue samples were collected at the operating theatre and transferred to the laboratory within 30 to 40 min in cooled sucrose based aCSF enriched with carbogen (95% O2, 5% CO2).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing slice preparation.

claim: Slice thickness was 400 µm for human tissue.
source: Slice thickness was 400 µm.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing slice preparation.

claim: Brain slices of 300 µm thickness were cut for rat experiments.
source: Brain slices of 300 µm thickness were cut on a Leica VT1200 vibratome (Leica Biosystems) and subsequently stored in the sucrose aCSF solution.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing rat slice preparation.

claim: Whole-cell recordings were performed at 34°C under submerged conditions.
source: Whole-cell recordings were performed at 34°C under submerged conditions, the bath chamber was perfused with an aCSF solution containing (in mM): 125 NaCl, 2.5 KCl, 1 MgCl2, 2 CaCl2, 10 glucose, 1.25 NaH2PO4, and 25 NaHCO3 (300 mOsm).
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing recording conditions.

claim: Data were low-pass filtered at 6 kHz using the built in four-pole Bessel filter and digitized at a sampling rate of 20 kHz.
source: Data were low-pass filtered at 6 kHz using the built in four-pole Bessel filter and digitized at a sampling rate of 20 kHz.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing data acquisition.

claim: Four action potentials were elicited in each cell at 20 Hz for synaptic connectivity screening.
source: For synaptic connectivity screening, all cells were recorded in current clamp mode and held near –60 mV by means of constant and adjusting current injection. Four action potentials were elicited in each cell at 20 Hz with 1–4 nA for 1–3 ms and postsynaptic responses in the other cells were detected in the averaged traces from 30 to 50 sweeps.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section describing the recording protocol.

claim: Postsynaptic responses were detected in the averaged traces from 30 to 50 sweeps.

claim: Successful recordings were defined by a sufficiently high seal-resistance, resting membrane potentials of the cells more negative than −50 mV, long-term recording stability, and the ability of the neurons to produce characteristic action potential patterns during sustained step depolarisations.
source: Successful recordings were defined by a sufficiently high seal-resistance, resting membrane potentials of the cells more negative than −50 mV (not corrected for liquid junction potential), long-term recording stability, and the ability of the neurons to produce characteristic action potential patterns during sustained step depolarisations.
evidence: Directly stated in the methods section defining quality criteria.
